anatomy-of-a-good-prompt.r: A prompt that said 'summarise this' produced different shapes of answer each time. Adding the audience, length, format and what to leave out made the output consistent enough to use.
anatomy-of-a-good-prompt.x: A prompt is a specification. State the task, context, constraints and output format, and include what to do when information is missing. Short is not the goal; unambiguous is.

examples-and-few-shot-prompting.r: A classification prompt kept mislabelling edge cases. Adding three examples, including a difficult one, improved accuracy more than rewriting the instructions.
examples-and-few-shot-prompting.x: Examples teach format and judgement, but they can also be copied too literally. Vary them, include edge cases and test whether the model generalises.

reasoning-and-step-by-step-prompts.r: A model gave wrong answers to multi-step questions until it was asked to work through the steps before answering. Accuracy improved, at the cost of more tokens and time.
reasoning-and-step-by-step-prompts.x: Step-by-step reasoning helps on some tasks and wastes tokens on others. Measure the gain, keep reasoning separate from the final answer you parse, and do not trust stated reasoning as proof.

system-prompts-roles-and-context-layout.r: A bot ignored its rules when users pasted long documents. Placing the instructions clearly in the system message and the documents in labelled sections kept it on task.
system-prompts-roles-and-context-layout.x: Structure prevents confusion: separate instructions from data, label sections and keep the order stable. Remember that anything in the context can influence behaviour, including untrusted text.

structured-output-json-and-schemas.r: A pipeline broke when the model added a friendly sentence before the JSON. Requesting a strict schema and parsing with validation made the output dependable.
structured-output-json-and-schemas.x: Use schemas and constrained output where available, validate everything, and decide what happens on failure. Keep schemas small, and version them like APIs.

validating-repairing-and-retrying-output.r: About two percent of outputs failed validation. A retry that included the validation error in the prompt fixed most of them, and the rest went to a human queue.
validating-repairing-and-retrying-output.x: Plan for invalid output as normal. Validate with code, retry with specific feedback a limited number of times, and measure the failure rate so you notice when it rises.

prompt-versioning-and-testing.r: A small wording change improved one case and quietly broke three others. A saved test set run on every prompt change showed the regression before release.
prompt-versioning-and-testing.x: Treat prompts like code: store them in version control, review changes, run a regression set and record which prompt version produced each output.

debugging-bad-prompts.r: An answer was wrong in a strange way. Simplifying the prompt step by step showed that an old instruction in the context contradicted the new one, and removing it fixed the behaviour.
debugging-bad-prompts.x: Reduce to the smallest prompt that fails, change one thing at a time and check for conflicts between instructions. Keep failing cases as tests so the problem stays fixed.
